_note: Each threat the platform defends against and the critical controls (critical_controls.json) that answer it (independent review, round 8, T-04). db/tools/critical_excerpts.py writes critical/THREAT_CONTROL_MAP.md with each control's test result in the same run, and fails the pack when a threat has no control or a control none of whose tests passed. A threat whose answer is not code (an external penetration test, a key service) names its launch gate instead.

threats.threat: A test or sandbox setting lowers a production server's safeguards
A server runs on a schema changed by hand
One company reads or writes another company's rows
A stolen password is enough to move money, widen access or export data
An instruction injected into the AI assistant makes a tool act beyond its policy
A database function runs with its owner's rights for anyone who calls it
A partner integration breaks silently when an event changes
Traffic to the database or the key service is read or forged on the network
A server is made to call an internal address or an unlisted host (SSRF, DNS rebinding)
An infected file is uploaded and served to another user
Audit records are altered or deleted to hide an action
A database copy or backup exposes identity numbers and personal data
Passwords are guessed, or the service is flooded
Emergency access is opened without control or never closed
A partner misses events and nobody is told
An attacker finds a weakness no internal test covers
The master key is lost or stolen
threats.gate: key service (KMS/HSM) and the key-loss drill
